authority: The exponent-separator property is "E" here, so "e" is passive; F&O 4.7.3 treats a matching character as an exponent-separator-sign only "if it is both preceded and followed within the sub-picture by an active character", and nothing follows this one. XPath 3.1 F&O 4.7.4: "The suffix is set to contain all passive characters to the right of the rightmost active character in the sub-picture". 99.5 rounds half-to-even to 100, and XPath 3.1 F&O 4.7.5: "If there is no decimal-separator character in the sub-picture, or if there are no digits to the right of the decimal-separator character in the string, then the decimal-separator character is removed from the string".
